A. With insufficient tools to fight COVID‑19, the United States mobilized all of society to insist on surviving the outbreak with the least disruption to the United States.
B. Minimize the impact of new variants on the United States by collecting and analyzing data on previous variants of COVID‑19 and strengthening regulation and review of specific variants.
C. Take specific measures for businesses and schools to provide businesses and schools to continue to operate through COVID-19 to reduce the cost and impact of the pandemic on the U.S. economy.
D. Expand global access to COVID-19 medicines, facilitate the formation of pharmaceutical research alliances, and increase global funding.

We evaluate that the national COVID-19 preparedness plan includes many elements discussing protecting against and treating COVID-19, testing, vaccination, emergency response, etc. Does that include the above elements? Also it seems to include a part about global vaccination and donation measures (expanding global access and high-level commitments). The plan includes "Expand global access to COVID-19 medicines, facilitating the formation of pharmaceutical research alliances and increasing global funding." This is part of US commitment to global health markets, some aspects of that are included in the Fact sheet.

However the statement asks if it is part of the plans. Actually, the plan doesn't explicitly mention "mobilized all of society to insist on surviving the outbreak with today least control." But the policy statement might be "The administration has put vaccines at the center of our COVID-19 response because of the tools." But to categorize it as part of the plan: it would be a statement about the plan's approach: We mobilized all of society, covering many. The plan includes the emphasis on controlling disruptions and large effect: "We have evidence of early action—vaccination, CMS, etc." Not sure there is that phrase.

Option B: "Minimize the impact of new variants on the United States by collecting and analyzing data on prior variants and strengthening regulation and review of specific variants." This is definitely part of the Plan's new variant section: they mention data collection, sequencing, global surveillance etc. So the plan includes (1) improved data and event detection; (2) variant playbook etc; (3) systemic improvement. So it is part of the plan.

Option C: "Take specific measures for businesses and schools to help them continue to operate through COVID-19 to reduce the cost and impact of the pandemic on the U.S. economy." This is there: the plan includes the section "Prevent economic and educational shutdowns". So context: Impact details regarding guidelines, testing, ventilation, and financial support. So yes.

Option D: "Expand global access to COVID-19 medicines, facilitate the formation of pharmaceutical research alliances, and increase global funding." This seems more like detail of the all-doses (5) "Focus on global health and vaccine production." So yes.

Thus which answer is not part of the plan? The letter from the set appears likely an answer: "A" is the one that not of the plan. But is there an explicit part of the plan referencing "mobilized all of society... minimal disruption etc." I'm not fully sure. Let's re-read: "The President in 2021…" The summary says: it mentions "The Administration has put funds, invested worldwide, and in 2025 budgets include funds." But the plan's "4 key goals" they mention "Protect against and treat COVID-19, ... estimated improvement records with no guarantee of minimal disruption." The plan includes "public-private partnerships that have fostered..."

I think the plan is official: "The final plan includes 4 key projects." The plan includes: "Protect against and treat COVID-19." Only "mobilize all of society" refers to a introduction and national mobilization.

Yes, as described: "The President’s National COVID-19 Preparedness Plan focuses on four key goals: protect against & treat COVID‑19, preserve the integrity of all institutions, ...?"
